methods.label: Read the positive side of the intercept
methods.explanation: \(y>0\) corresponds to the graph being above the x-axis. Since \(y\) increases as \(x\) increases, this occurs to the right of the intersection, that is, \(x>-2\).
methods.levelReason: The intercept and increasing behavior are supplied, so only the Grade 8 graph-inequality connection and basic coordinate interpretation are needed.

methods.label: Solve the inequality algebraically
methods.explanation: Subtracting \(4\) from both sides isolates the term containing \(x\): \(2x>-4\). Dividing by the positive number \(2\) keeps the inequality direction unchanged. Since the original inequality is strict, the solution set is \(x>-2\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: This distinct algebraic route uses only Grade 7 inequality solving, with division by a positive number.
